name: MATADOR
description: Matador (meaning 'killer' or bullfighter) is a unique domino game from Spain with special matching rules. Unlike standard dominoes where matching numbers touch, in Matador the touching ends must add up to seven. The 'matador' tiles (0-0, 1-6, 2-5, 3-4) can be played on any end, giving the game its name. Also known as 'Russian Dominoes' or 'Kardinal domino' in some regions.

A Spanish game whose name literally means 'killing' or bullfighter. The same game is also called 'Russian Dominoes' in some English books and 'Kardinal domino' in Germany for unknown reasons.
2-4 players, individually or in partnerships. With 4 players, can play as individuals or partnerships.
Standard double-six domino set (28 tiles). Each player gets 7 tiles.

items.text: Double-9: Play with double-9 set (55 tiles); touching ends add to 10; six matadors are 0-0 and tiles totalling 10 (1-9, 2-8, 3-7, 4-6, 5-5).
Double-12: Play with double-12 set (91 tiles); touching ends add to 13; seven matadors are 0-0 and tiles totalling 13 (1-12 through 6-7).
Leyden: Matador variant with cross-shaped layout: four arms radiating from the initial double.
Matadors crosswise (optional): Any matador may be played across the line; next player chooses which end of the matador is the new train end. In two-player, can force opponent to miss a turn.
Matadors crosswise on blank: When a matador is played on a blank, it must be played crosswise; next tile on that end must have blank as inward end. Anglo-Saxon variant.
